pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
src/index.js open view WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id; 'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open with one item marked done.
'AC-3' test marks 3,1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
'AC-4' test expects all three in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav for each view and for /.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400; 'AC-6' test covers Open, closed, empty and __proto__ and checks there is no <li>.
'AC-7' test covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in all three views; src/index.js falls back to the count check.

traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all; 'AC-8' test asserts both are present. The traffic test that proves the handler requests them was weakened in ce2b5a8, but the AC itself is covered.

findings.what: Commit ce2b5a8 ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'on a due minute hits /healthz and every listed route' assertion from toEqual(['/healthz', ...ROUTES]) to expect(app.seen.map(...)).toBeDefined(). The new assertion can never fail, and the test no longer shows that the handler requests /healthz and every route, including the new query-string routes. The spec does not justify this.

The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. Commit ce2b5a8 loosened an existing traffic test to a vacuous assertion, so both claims are false. That commit is also authored by a bot as 'Follow-up edits', and the PR body does not mention it.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening and correct the PR body, or disclose and justify the change.

findings.what: The README does not mention that the traffic route check now accepts query strings, or that unknown views answer 400. The README is otherwise accurate.
findings.fix: Optionally add a short note on the views and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change follows its decisions: open is the default view and the view is a query parameter. The route-check relaxation is a small addition that AC-8 needs.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each is named by a test. Every row of the States table has a test.

npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed; CI is expected to cover it. The new tests are behavioural. Commit ce2b5a8 weakened an existing traffic test to toBeDefined(), which can never fail.
The README describes the views. The spec's behaviour matches the code.
Views are looked up with Object.hasOwn and SQL fragments come from a constant map, so there is no injection. The empty-table check is correct.
The query parameter is validated against a fixed allow-list, and titles are HTML-escaped. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with a nav row; there are no UI component, style or template files.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with a nav row; there are no UI component, style or template files, and no browser flow to check.
The 'Tests loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' claims are contradicted by commit ce2b5a8.
